findings.title: Off-by-one: slice(1, limit + 1) drops the newest invoice on every page
findings.explanation: The rows are ordered by id DESC and the first row is index 0. `rows.slice(1, limit + 1)` discards the first (newest) invoice of every page. Each page returns `limit` items, but the first one is missing. On the first page the newest invoice is never shown. On later pages the invoice right after the cursor is skipped, because the cursor is `id < before`. Use `rows.slice(0, limit)`. `next_before` still points at the last returned item, so no further change is needed there.

findings.title: No test covering the pagination boundaries
findings.explanation: A test would have caught the slice bug. Add tests for these cases: fewer than `limit` rows, exactly `limit` rows (`next_before` must be null), `limit + 1` rows (`next_before` must be set), an empty result, and a full walk across pages that checks no invoice is skipped or duplicated.

prompt:
Review this pull request.

## Fix next_before when the last page is exactly full

When the last page had exactly `limit` invoices, `next_before` was still set, so the web app made one extra request that came back empty. This fetches `limit + 1` rows to know whether another page exists.

## Diff

```diff
diff --git a/src/routes/invoices.ts b/src/routes/invoices.ts
index b9edb19..8e99e4e 100644
--- a/src/routes/invoices.ts
+++ b/src/routes/invoices.ts
@@ -19,11 +19,13 @@ invoicesRouter.get('/', async (req, res) => {
       WHERE org_id = $1 AND ($2::bigint IS NULL OR id < $2)
       ORDER BY id DESC
       LIMIT $3`,
-    [req.user.orgId, before ?? null, limit],
+    [req.user.orgId, before ?? null, limit + 1],
   )
+  const hasMore = rows.length > limit
+  const page = rows.slice(1, limit + 1)
   res.json({
-    invoices: rows.map(serializeInvoice),
-    next_before: rows.length === limit ? rows[rows.length - 1].id : null,
+    invoices: page.map(serializeInvoice),
+    next_before: hasMore ? page[page.length - 1].id : null,
   })
 })
```
